MISSIONIRY FROM WYCLIFFE. The Work Of A Past Member In India Extolled. The -good work Of the London Missionary Society is well-known to the people of Wycliffe Congregational Church, and a deputation, con- sisting of Miss Kathleen Morris, of North India, and the Rev. Henry Robertson, of China, had a hearty welcome last week-end. ' The opening meeting took place in the Memorial Hall, Mr. Edward Wallington pre- siding. With him on the platform *ere the Rev. T. T. James and the deputation. The Chairman remarked upon the great interest which • that Chnrch had always taken in missionary work, and pointed out that the,great old- man of the missionary movement, the Rev. Dr. Moffat, of South African fame, received his first inspiration for missionary work at a meet- ing held in Flag-lane Chapel, which, along with the meeting room at the Nag's Head, formed the early pages in the history of Wycliffe Con- gregational Church. (Applause.) They had also produced a missionary from their members, the Rev. Arthur Dignum, who at one time was •a scholar in Wycliffe Church Sunday School with himself (Mr. Wallington). Mr. Dignum died at a very early age, but the result of his work was still to be seen. Every year they had sent a donation to help to maintain the school which Mr. Dignum established at Warn, in South India. (Applause.y In the' course of his address, the Rev. Henry Robertson pointed out what a great difficulty missionaries had to contend with in the ignor- ance of the Chinese and their unwillingness to lead a purer and better life, which was a Christian necessity. Miss Morris, who was attired in a long flowing Indian robe, related' -some interesting exper- iences of her life in North India. Where she worked, she said the result; were not too good, but the missionaries were determined to stick to their work and hoped for better things in the future. The services were continued on Sunday, when the preacher in the morning was the Rev. T. T. James, and in the evening Miss Morris. WELCOMED BY BLACK CHIEF. Interesting Narrative At Legh Street By Missionary. The missionary services at the Legh-street Primitive Methodist Church last week-end were interesting throughout. Financially, they were also successful, the collections being nearly double last year's amount., . The services were commenced on Saturday evening, when a meeting of, welcome to tht. deputation, the Rev. J. R. and. Mrs. Fell, from Kanchindu, Africa; was held. Giving an account of his work, the reverend gentleman said that on the occasion of his first visit to Africa he was very unwelcome, the natives running away from all white men. On the second occasion, however, he was heartily welcomed, being met by the Chief himself. They had opened seven new places during the year, and they had now ' forty-seven preaching stations along the Ztembesi river, and ten others where they occasionally preached. The day schools had doubled in number, although they had a great difficulty in getting the girls to attend. They had two hundred scholars at- tending the schools, and five girls in residence as boarders. Mrs. Fell had also done some im- portant work, teaching sewing and household -work. They had taken an orphan baby into their keeping, which they had rescued on the point of death. In that part of the country they killed the babies when the mother died, thinking that the mother wanted the children wjth her where she was going. Services were held at the Church on Sunday. the Rev. J. R. Fell preaching both morning and evening. In the evening an anthem, "Who- soever drinketh of this water" (Field), was nicely rendered by the choir, Mr. J. Dakin sing- ing a bass solo. Mr. T. Tanner presided at the organ. The annual missionary meeting was held at Legh-street on Monday evening, being presided over by Mrs. A. L. Bridge (Liverpool). A missionary enthuiast, who is in close touch with the Missionary Federation in this district, Mrs. Irvane, came over as secretary of the association, and a new branch .in connection with the circuit was formed, on her proposi- tion. The services were concluded at Knutsford-road on Tuesday evening, when both missionaries again spoke.
